Reopen PR #4386 @ d73fa0c7b. Independently reproduced 613 passed/162 subtests on the exact PR head, confirmed no origin/dev content is reverted by the 850a8c760 merge (merge-tree clean; _canonical_task_agent_pairs and reap_stale_l12_missing_process_failure_streaks are new on dev, not deleted here), config.json untouched, git diff --check clean, and all 7 items from the previous reopen landed. AC3 (stale-failure guard + record_stale_worker_failure_reassignment_skip) is correct. Blocking on the new active-termination path in reconcile_worker_task_assignments:

(1) It kills live workers whose owner/reviewer never changed. worker_matches_current_assignment returns False for ANY task status outside owned/review/finalize -- including the canonical `blocked` status -- and for archived (done) tasks. Every False is classified `authoritative_task_assignment_changed`, so the worker is SIGTERM/SIGKILLed, set to superseded with exit_code 143, its queue lease finalized, and an activity event asserts the row "no longer authorizes its dispatch identity" -- which is false. Reproduced with the new suite's own harness: task {owner Claude2, reviewer Antigravity} unchanged, worker agent claude2, status moved to `blocked` -> terminate_worker_pid(4242), status superseded, exit 143, worker_assignment_reconciled written. Same for a worker that just ran `done` and had its row archived. Any worker that records a blocker, and every owner finishing closeout, is now killed on the next cycle.

(2) It bypasses active_worker_governance_lease_decision. That guard exists precisely to decide whether canonical governance truth may end an active lease, and it returns preserve/`governance_only_transition` for the `blocked` case and preserve/`missing_or_ambiguous_task_truth` for the archived case (both verified directly). Because the reconciler is wired as a pre-dispatch reserved phase BEFORE the worker poll, it preempts that guard and also preempts poll_workers' graceful done-task path, which marks such a worker `completed` rather than `superseded`.

(3) PID-reuse unsafe termination. It calls terminate_worker_pid(worker.get("pid")) with no expected_start_ticks, while the existing assignment-mismatch path uses terminate_worker_process_generation(worker). terminate_worker_pid documents that without Linux's start-ticks token a reused PID is indistinguishable from the intended worker (its deferred path fails closed for exactly this). Worker records already carry pid_start_ticks/process_generation; ignoring them means a stale record with a recycled PID gets an unrelated process SIGTERM->SIGKILLed and then records exit_code 143 as if the worker was terminated.

(4) Coverage gap that hid this: test_live_worker_for_previous_owner_is_superseded_with_exact_evidence only exercises a genuine owner change (dispatch Codex2 vs row Claude2). Please add tests that pin (a) an owner-unchanged worker on a non-dispatch status such as `blocked` is preserved, (b) a done/archived-row worker keeps the existing completed path, and (c) termination is bound to the captured process generation.

Requested fix: restrict the terminate/supersede action to a genuine owner/reviewer identity change (compare task_assignment_at_dispatch against the current row rather than reusing worker_matches_current_assignment's dispatch-eligibility semantics), route it through active_worker_governance_lease_decision, and terminate via terminate_worker_process_generation. Reporting-only rows can keep the current join.
